seoTitle: Adverb and Weak Word Highlighter for Writers
metaDescription: Mark -ly adverbs and weak qualifiers like very, really and just in your draft, with counts and a rate per 100 words. Free and private.
intro: Mark -ly adverbs and weak words like very, really, just and quite in your draft, with counts and a rate per 100 words.
why:
Many editors advise cutting adverbs and softeners that prop up a weak verb. A very big house is a mansion, and she walked slowly may be she crept.

This tool marks every word ending in -ly (except a list of common non-adverbs) and a list of qualifiers such as very, really, quite and just. It counts them per 100 words so you can compare drafts. It is a word-list check, not grammar: it will miss adverbs without -ly and flag some good ones.
howTo: Choose whether to flag -ly words, qualifiers or both.
Read the marked text and the table.

faq.a: No. Adverbs like often or fast do not end in -ly, and some -ly words are adjectives. It is a list-based check.

faq.q: Should I remove all of them?
faq.a: No. Use them when they add meaning. The count is there to prompt a second look.
